*[Bug 19140] X11 segfault*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19140>

Ivan Krylov (<mailto:ikrylov@disroot.org|ikrylov@disroot.org>) changed:

           What    |Removed                     |Added
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                 CC|                            |ikrylov@disroot.org

--- Comment #2 from Ivan Krylov (<mailto:ikrylov@disroot.org|ikrylov@disroot.org>) ---
Thankfully this is not a documented interface, because there are other code
paths that don't validate the `display` string:

```
# overflow in strcpy(tmp, dsp+6)
jpeg(strrep("a", 9999), type = "Xlib")
tiff(strrep("a", 9999), type = "Xlib")
x11(paste0('jpeg::42:', strrep('a', 9999)))
x11(paste0('tiff::42:', strrep('a', 9999)))
```

Only `jpeg` and `tiff` are susceptible because of the need to pass an
additional number (JPEG quality, TIFF compression) before the file path.

Technically, `xd->quality = atoi(dsp+6);` invokes undefined behaviour in cases
like `jpeg::99999999999999999:foo`, but that will surface only with sanitized
builds when using the undocumented interface.

Even if the string is well-formed, the bitmap device still doesn't work when
initialised by a call to `x11(type = "cairo")`:

```
x11("jpeg::42:/dev/null", 200, 200, type = "cairo"); plot.new()
x11("tiff::1:/dev/null", 200, 200, type = "cairo"); plot.new()
x11("png::/dev/null", 200, 200, type = "cairo"); plot.new()
x11("bmp::/dev/null", 200, 200, type = "cairo"); plot.new()
```

`xd->cc` is only initialised if `type == WINDOW`, so in pixmap cases it stays a
null pointer, causing the following call to Cairo to crash.

Perhaps it's best for `x11()` to detect and forbid such syntax altogether? But
then things like `DISPLAY='[::1]:0'` should still work. It might be more
reliable to change the arguments to `.External2(C_X11, ...)` to pass device
type / quality / file path / display address separately.

*[Bug 19141] New: `<http://is.na|is.na>()` and the `as.*()` coercions read their argument one element at a time*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19141>

            Bug ID: 19141
           Summary: `<http://is.na|is.na>()` and the `as.*()` coercions read their
                    argument one element at a time
           Product: R
           Version: R-devel (trunk)
          Hardware: Other
                OS: Other
            Status: NEW
          Severity: normal
          Priority: P5
         Component: Wishlist
          Assignee: <mailto:R-core@R-project.org|R-core@R-project.org>
          Reporter: <mailto:kevinushey@gmail.com|kevinushey@gmail.com>

Created attachment 3796
  --> <https://bugs.r-project.org/attachment.cgi?id=3796&action=edit>
Candidate patch.

## Summary

`do_isna()` and the `coerceTo*()` functions read their argument through the
element-at-a-time accessors:

```
    case REALSXP:
        for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
            pa[i] = ISNAN(REAL_ELT(x, i));
        break;
```

`REAL_ELT()` inlines to `ALTREP(x) ? ALTREAL_ELT(x, i) : REAL0(x)[i]`. For an
ALTREP argument that is a virtual dispatch per element. For *any* argument it
is a per-element branch on the object header which the compiler cannot hoist
past the writes to `pa`, so the loop does not vectorise.

`anyNA()` -- thirty lines further down the same file -- does not have this
problem, because it reads by region:

```
        ITERATE_BY_REGION(x, xD, i, nbatch, double, REAL, {
                for (int k = 0; k < nbatch; k++)
                    if (ISNAN(xD[k]))
                        return true;
            });
```

The reason for the difference looks accidental: `#include <R_ext/Itermacros.h>`
sits at `coerce.c:2435`, immediately above `anyNA()` and *below* `do_isna()`,
so `ITERATE_BY_REGION` was simply not in scope where `<http://is.na|is.na>()` is written.

The same shape appears in fourteen loops across `coerceToLogical()`,
`coerceToInteger()`, `coerceToReal()` and `coerceToComplex()`.

## Reproducer

```
n <- 1e7
tim <- function(e) {
    ex <- substitute(e); pf <- parent.frame(); eval(ex, pf)
    round(1000 * min(replicate(3,
        system.time(for (.i in 1:20) eval(ex, pf))[["elapsed"]])) / 20, 1)
}
mat <- function(x) x[seq_along(x)]          # force materialization

i_alt <- seq_len(n);        i_mat <- mat(i_alt)
d_alt <- as.numeric(i_alt); d_mat <- mat(d_alt)
lgl   <- rep_len(c(TRUE, FALSE, NA), n)

c(is.na_altrep_int = tim(<http://is.na|is.na>(i_alt)), is.na_int  = tim(<http://is.na|is.na>(i_mat)),
  is.na_altrep_dbl = tim(<http://is.na|is.na>(d_alt)), is.na_dbl  = tim(<http://is.na|is.na>(d_mat)),
  as.numeric_int   = tim(as.numeric(i_mat)),
  as.logical_int   = tim(as.logical(i_mat)),
  anyNA_int        = tim(anyNA(i_mat)),   # reads by region already
  baseline_d_plus0 = tim(d_mat + 0))
```

Times in ms for one call on 10^7 elements. Both columns are the same trunk
r90424 build on the same machine (macOS 15 / arm64, clang), with and without
the patch, so they differ only by the change. Released R 4.6.1 gives the same
left-hand column to within run-to-run noise.

| | r90424 | + patch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<http://is.na|is.na>(seq_len(n))` (ALTREP) | 12.6 | **1.1** |
| `<http://is.na|is.na>(<integer>)` | 2.9 | **0.8** |
| `<http://is.na|is.na>(as.numeric(1:n))` (ALTREP) | 12.4 | **2.0** |
| `<http://is.na|is.na>(<double>)` | 2.9 | **1.3** |
| `<http://is.na|is.na>(<logical>)` | 2.9 | **0.8** |
| `<http://is.na|is.na>(<complex>)` | 2.9 | 2.7 |
| `as.numeric(<integer>)` | 4.4 | **1.4** |
| `as.logical(<integer>)` | 3.9 | **0.9** |
| `as.numeric(<logical>)` | 4.4 | **1.6** |
| `as.logical(<double>)` | 3.3 | **1.6** |
| `as.numeric(<raw>)` | 4.2 | **2.7** |
| `as.complex(<double>)` | 3.4 | **2.3** |
| `as.integer(<double>)` | 6.0 | **4.0** |
| `as.numeric(<complex>)` | 5.0 | 5.0 |
| *`anyNA(<integer>)`, for contrast* | *2.4* | *2.4* |
| *`d + 0`, for scale* | *1.4* | *1.5* |

The materialized cases improve as well, so this is not only about ALTREP.
The two that do not move are already memory-bound at 16 bytes an element;

`as.integer(<double>)` gains least because `IntegerFromReal()`'s range checks
dominate. Nothing measured got slower.

## Patch

Two parts.

`<http://is.na|is.na>()`: move the `Itermacros.h` include to the top of the file and switch
the four atomic branches of `do_isna()` to `ITERATE_BY_REGION`, exactly as
`anyNA()` already does.

The coercions: the fourteen loops have one shape -- run an element converter
over the source -- so they go through a single `COERCE_BY_REGION` macro
rather than fourteen copies of the same iteration (net -56 lines).
`coerceToString()` is left alone because there is no `STRING_GET_REGION`, and
`coerceToRaw()` because it does its range handling inline rather than calling
a converter, so it does not fit the macro.

No behaviour changes.


## Related, not in this patch

`ISNA()` costs about 6x what the same test costs inlined, because `R_IsNA()`
is an exported out-of-line function that package code cannot inline through.
Over 10^7 doubles: `ISNA()` 9.1 ms, the identical payload test inlined 1.5 ms,
`ISNAN()` 1.1 ms (it inlines to `isnan()`). Giving `ISNA` an inline definition
in the header, while keeping the function exported for ABI, would close that.
